title: Rep. Chuck Edwards drops re-election bid after House censure recommendation
dek: Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., withdrew from his re-election campaign on August 5, 2026, days after the House Ethics Committee recommended censure over sexual harassment allegations involving two female staffers. The bipartisan committee found Edwards engaged in unprofessional conduct but found no evidence of sexual activity, quid pro quo harassment, or violations of federal law.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Edwards announced his withdrawal from re-election on August 5, 2026, two days after the House Ethics Committee recommended censure for persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct toward two young female staffers.
bottom_line: The full House has not yet voted on the Ethics Committee's censure recommendation. That vote may proceed despite Edwards' departure, or his withdrawal may render it moot depending on House procedures. Watch whether the full chamber chooses to formally censure a departing member.
body: Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., announced his withdrawal from re-election on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, two days after the House Ethics Committee recommended censure over allegations of sexual harassment involving two female staffers.
Edwards stated: "After much prayer and reflection, I've decided to withdraw from my re-election campaign. I will complete my current term." He is 65 years old.

On Monday, August 3, the bipartisan Ethics Committee recommended that the full House censure Edwards after finding that he "engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers." The 25-page report concluded that "Representative Edwards violated the House Code of Official Conduct by failing to adhere to the spirit of rules prohibiting sexual harassment of and unwanted advances to House staffers."

The committee's findings detailed a pattern of behavior that included "providing the young women with lavish and recurrent gifts, making comments regarding their appearance and dress, inviting them to intimate dinners and vacations, sending notes regarding his effusive affection, and inviting them to other activities as a way to spend time together." However, the committee found no evidence that Edwards engaged in sexual activity with or propositioned any of his staffers. The allegations, per the committee, "do not implicate quid pro quo sexual harassment" or violate "the letter of federal sexual harassment law."

Edwards denied that any of his actions were intended to be sexual or romantic in nature and cooperated with the investigation. His counsel filed a 15-page rebuttal to the committee's findings, calling them "unfounded." Edwards previously called the allegations "baseless" and stated in May 2026 that he welcomed an investigation.
Edwards won the Republican primary in 2022 against then-Rep. Madison Cawthorn. His withdrawal reshapes the race for North Carolina's 11th District, a competitive seat held by Republicans.
